First pre-release of 2.1 — **adding books**. Bookbench can now bring new books into your library and keep the main copy on your computer instead of only on the e-reader.

## New

- **Add books** (*File > Add books …*, Ctrl+I, or drag EPUB files and folders onto the window): a list with title, author, series and where each book will go. Check and change title, authors, author sort, series, number and ISBN before copying; the original file stays untouched.
- **Duplicates** are found by Calibre ID, ISBN, or title and author. Per book: *Add*, *Skip*, *Replace existing* (keeps the file name, so KOReader keeps the reading position and highlights; a backup is made first) or *Keep both*.
- **Folder scheme** with Calibre placeholders, e.g. `{author_sort}/[{series}/][{series_index:2} - ]{title}`. Bookbench detects the scheme your books already follow; change it under *Settings > Books > Library and import*. Existing books are never moved or renamed.
- **New library from e-reader** (*File* menu): copies all books of the connected e-reader into a folder on your computer with the same structure. KOReader's `.sdr` folders stay on the e-reader. The library folder gets a small `.bookbench` folder, so the settings travel with it (also in a folder synced between Windows and Linux).
- **Reading cache:** unchanged books are not read again when a library opens.

Coming in the next betas: removing advert lines (OceanofPDF and the like) and copying new or changed books to the e-reader.

## Install

- **Linux:** *Help > Check for updates* in an installed copy (with *Settings > Updates > Include pre-releases* on), or `install.sh` from this repository.
- **Windows:** `Bookbench_Setup_2.1-beta1.exe` (not signed yet: SmartScreen > *More info* > *Run anyway*).
